title: The Hateful Hometown
subtitle: Once tangled in a single arrangement, now unraveling in a sea of melodies.

items.text: Cumulus clouds drift slowly across the night sky like the rolling waves of the sea, the countless stars glinting gently behind them.
Captain's Cabin
The damp sea breeze has laid a heavy layer of moisture on the surfaces of the ship. Standing at the observation window, the captain's face betrays no emotion.
There is a faint, hesitant sound at her door.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Oh, Ms. Fatutu, I hadn't expected you to visit.
Grace's face lights up, every inch radiating joy.
She eagerly opens the door, affectionately pulling Fatutu into the room.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: I must say it's a welcome relief from the onslaught of greedy businessmen and boorish officials.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: All puff and no substance—bloated, lifeless, they remind me of a few specimens of decay from my collection.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Decaying specimens? Ms. Grace, you mean bodi—

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Hush. Let's just leave things at that.
She squints as she studies the faintly protruding veins on the girl's hands, imagining the blood coursing anxiously through them.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: So then, you're here to talk about something else? Go ahead.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Yes, Ms. Grace.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I just wanted some advice, if you don't mind.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Not at all, my dear. We are friends, aren't we?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: We are venturing into the unknown. So, it is little surprise that you feel lost, but disorientation is a dangerous enemy. I am more than happy to help.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Relax and keep an open mind, dear. We have a long night ahead.
A few soft, subtle noises come from outside, but they are not enough to disrupt the intimate conversation between the two.
Grace sets down her pocket watch, her gaze drifting past the slightly ajar door, a faint smile teasing her lips.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The thing is, I tried to ignore the outside world, just like you said, but I failed.
Fatutu instinctively lowers her head.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The idea of raising a spear against people I know so little about, even if it was to avenge my home.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I thought I had to learn more about these outsiders, to understand them. I'm sorry I went against your advice.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I thought that learning about them would harden my resolve.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I thought that I would hate them from the depths of my soul, that the hatred would be so strong that I'd feel no remorse, that I would see in them what you and Manus Vindictae do.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: But ...
In the face of her wavering resolve, Fatutu bows her head in shame.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Instead, after interacting with the people here ...
The noisy music hall, the bustling tourists, the bright lights, the sea shanties—they all linger in her mind.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Fatutu, my dear. There's no shame in having second thoughts.
The gentleness of her response leaves Fatutu momentarily stunned.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: How could you not? This was but your first glimpse of a world so much wider than you knew.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: But you'll soon realize that it is nothing more than a dying corpse, its lungs still clinging on to its last breath.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: The face rots first, you know? It's a nasty scene, I assure you. Those shrinking, putrefying eyeballs are always a headache for taxidermists.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Next, the chest cavity. It rots out from the inside, bloating with noxious gases produced by its decomposing flesh until it's ready to pop like a party balloon.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Even at this stage, if you were to hold your breath and look only to the limbs, you might marvel at the artisanship—such a perfect creation! Yet, it dies all the same. So it goes.
Fatutu has never encountered such a warm and spirited captain before.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Do you see the world any clearer now? Take your time. Think it through.
Grace lightly taps her finger on the board beside her, as if keeping time with the faint footsteps outside.
Lost in thought, Fatutu remains oblivious to it all.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The outsiders are different from what I expected. Ms. Grace, are you sure they're truly evil?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Heh heh.
Grace glances out the window.
Through the porthole, a strange vibrating sound grows louder and more distinct.
Following Grace's gaze, Fatutu notices an enormous "shadow" on the other side of the porthole.
Can parasols and railings really create such an enormous silhouette?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: They're cunning, menacing, and at times, have even been known to engage in eavesdropping.
The "shadow" creeps closer toward them, stealthy and deliberate.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: M-Ms. Grace, watch out! It's ... it's some kind of monster!
There is no doubt. This cutting description has angered the shadowy intruder.
Huh?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I-It's here!
Scrambling, Fatutu grabs whatever is nearby—signal lights, brooms, and heaving lines—and flings them out the door.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'll protect you, Ms. Grace!
The commotion seems to have come to an end.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Is it dead?
Panting heavily, Fatutu musters the courage to rush out of the cabin.
The figure on the deck is far removed from the terrifying enemy she envisioned.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Oh! It's you, Barcarola.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: *sob*
A familiar tear-streaked face emerges from the aftermath of the chaos.
The captain, however, seems unfazed by the disheveled state of her cruise staff.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Ms. Barcarola, what a pleasure to see you.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Have you lost your mind, Fatutu?!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I've been looking all over the ship for you to thank you for the lamps you made!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: This is a funny way of saying "you're welcome."

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Not even the rudest stunad in Cremona would attack someone for saying thanks!
An unfamiliar term springs from her lips, sparking Fatutu's curiosity.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Cremona? Where's that?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: That's really not what matters here!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Settle down please, ladies. This was only a small misunderstanding, wasn't it?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: As both your captain and your friend, I hope that you might be able to resolve this. I do believe I could see you two becoming fast friends.
The captain's overtures are anything but subtle.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Fatutu here is eager to learn about the outside world. And I'm sure you must have many stories to share, don't you?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Consider it a favor in exchange for those Sea Mother's Eyes.
It simply wouldn't do for a captain to leave these two in such a state.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Why don't you take a seat, Ms. Barcarola?
She moves aside, extending two delicate hands to them.
The girls take her hands, allowing themselves to be drawn close. Then, they lean together on the railing.
The sea breeze sweeps across the deck, dispersing whatever awkwardness there was between them.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: You were quick to gloss over your hometown. Cremona, wasn't it?
Grace's voice is gentle and soft. Barcarola finally loosens the tension in her strings, speaking as she looks out over the moonlit water.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Cremona, the "City of Violins," as they say. Sì, I was born in that awful, dreary old place. But I don't like to talk about it, Ms. Grace.
Fatutu examines Barcarola's expression.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Hmm. But it sounds like you still miss your home, so why speak of it that way? Is there something wrong with it?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: In Nukutaeao, when we find something rotted in our village, we wrap it up in stinky grass and throw it in the ocean.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Do you outsiders not do this as well?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: W-Well, it's not completely rotted exactly. It's just ...
She furrows her brow, seemingly searching for the right words.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: In Cremona, everything is bound up with the violin. How it's made, how it's played, even the science of it. It fills the air, and every conversation. You can't walk to the restaurant without tripping over a virtuoso!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: They come from Rome, Berlin, London, New York, Nairobi, Tokyo, Uppsala, people from far and wide, all crammed into one town. Not a day goes by without a concert, a symphony, or a festival musicale.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Am I misunderstanding you? Because to the Nukutai, the idea of a place with music and festivals every day sounds very fun.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: That's where you're wrong, Miss. It's no fun at all.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: At least, for me. To be Cremonese is to take pride in its music, its history, and above all, its violins.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: And you must learn to love the violin, the viola, the violoncello, and the bass! Because there is nothing else! Every quartet is a string quartet. Every concerto is Vivaldi! Strings, strings, strings! The monotony is unbearable!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: The world has so very many instruments as diverse and as varied as the people that fill it! Even the shell around your neck could sing if you knew just where to tap it!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But not in Cremona. That's why I speak of it that way, Fatutu. Because, if I had stayed there, I would never have seen the music of the world and its instruments, and my Crackling Box would never have been able to know their sounds.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The Nukutai don't have many instruments—not so many as you anyway—but we were never bored with what we had.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'm certain that your island holds great beauty beyond its music. If ever we grow tired of singing and dancing, we'd go searching for shells or swimming in the reefs.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: *sigh* You still have much to learn about the world beyond your islands.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Then you have no intention of ever returning home, Ms. Barcarola?
A seemingly most ordinary question.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Return? No, never!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: They're too set in their ways, like old fossils. My vision of music grew beyond them, and I did too.
Barcarola cups her hands around her mouth and hollers out into the fog-covered horizon.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I won't force myself back into their little world!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Your determination is admirable indeed.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Glad to hear it. Then my position is safe for another day.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: How could it not be? You are the very star of the "Free Breeze."

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Uh-huh!
Barcarola's face lights up with renewed pride.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: What about you, Ms. Grace?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: You've never told us about your home.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: It's a place of little interest to anyone, not even worthy of naming.
Her demeanor is far more composed than the rambling chatter of Barcarola.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: They say a musician must be free of attachments to be truly creative. Perhaps this is true of captains as well.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: No. That can't be right!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The Nukutai believe that to stray from our home is the death of the spirit. If we travel too far and too long, our Spirit Shells develop cracks that no amount of Nukuglue can mend.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: And from these cracks come an intense sadness, the elders call it ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Home sick.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Homesickness—sì, we have this word as well. The sailors aboard often ask me to play the songs of their youth when they are missing their homes. So many different melodies. Thankfully, my Crackling Box has all kinds of instruments to suit their needs.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I imagine it must be difficult for your people now.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: If you'd like, I could learn to play some of your songs and perform them. I'd be more than happy to help, after all you've done.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: That's kind of you.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'm sure it will be of great help to us.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I'm more than happy to help, Fatutu! It is my job, after all!
The girls' conversation seems to stretch on forever, but the increasing frequency with which they rub their eyes clearly marks the passage of time.
Eventually, the sun climbs above the sea, painting its surface a satin blue, and, as the ship's horn sounds, gentle ripples spread across its surface.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: It appears the sun has caught up with us, ladies.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Mamma mia! The concert!
As she rubs her eyes, Barcarola catches a glimpse of the captain lightly shaking her pocket watch and remembers something equally important.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I promised Ms. Regulus a rock-and-roll concert. But I haven't even asked her what instruments she needs!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Bye, girls!
With hurried footsteps clattering down the stairs, Barcarola quickly vanishes.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Thank you for talking with us, Ms. Grace.
She has waited for Barcarola to be clearly out of sight before speaking.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Don't mention it. I only hope that it was helpful for you.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I-I have one last question.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I was wondering how do you stay so determined?
